scope: Re-run browser, visual, and runtime certification against the exact independently certified Draco/CSP correction candidate.
Build and launch the production preview from the exact candidate SHA without modifying application, GLB, decoder, CSP, Blender, topology, content, or deployment state.
Capture desktop 1440x1000, 1024x768, mobile 390x844, and forced non-WebGL evidence after the Command Center GLB and local Draco JS decoder have settled.
Prove the browser requests /draco/draco_decoder.js successfully from same-origin, does not request Google/gstatic Draco assets, and emits no WebAssembly/CSP decoder failures.
Prove the certified Command Center GLB now renders in the actual browser and the prior procedural/fallback presentation is no longer the dominant scene.
Exercise Ask interaction, movement readability, map/HUD usability, at least one SPA exit, network/error state, and responsive overflow.

stop_conditions: The certified Draco/CSP correction ref no longer resolves to b5e27e729e6481bc98875177057fc0a193aef7ce.
The production GLB hash/size or local decoder hash/size differs from the certified values.
The browser attempts to load an external Draco decoder or uses WebAssembly for Command Center decoding.
The GLB request succeeds but authored scenery still does not render.
An application page error, unexpected console error, failed request, or unexpected HTTP failure appears and is not a known harmless headless-browser environment warning.
The authored scene materially obscures spawn, Ask, HUD, bridge entrances, movement readability, or required interaction cues.
The visual result materially diverges from the certified Blender intent or is broken after integration.
Fixing any discovered issue would require modifying a protected application/asset path; preserve evidence and STOP for a separate correction task.
Independent Terra review returns fix_required or stop.
